about.tagline: Automatic transcripts for UN Web TV meetings.

whatIsThis.heading: What is this?
whatIsThis.body: UN Web TV Transcripts is a public preview tool that automatically generates searchable text transcripts from United Nations meeting recordings published on <webtvLink>UN Web TV</webtvLink>.

whoIsItFor.heading: Who is it for?
whoIsItFor.intro: The tool is designed to help anyone who needs quick access to the spoken content of UN meetings, including:
whoIsItFor.item1: Diplomats and delegation staff following proceedings across multiple organs
whoIsItFor.item2: Researchers and academics studying UN debates and voting records
whoIsItFor.item4: Civil society organisations monitoring policy discussions
whoIsItFor.item5: UN Secretariat staff reviewing meeting records

coverage.heading: What meetings are covered?
coverage.intro: The tool covers public meetings recorded and published on UN Web TV, including:
coverage.item1: Security Council (SC) — open meetings and briefings
coverage.item2: General Assembly (GA) — plenary and main committee sessions
coverage.item5: Other inter-governmental bodies as available on Web TV
coverage.closed: Closed or confidential meetings are not recorded on Web TV and are therefore not covered.

howItWorks.heading: How it works
howItWorks.step1Body: The system monitors UN Web TV for newly published meeting recordings. Meeting metadata — title, date, UN organ, and document references — is extracted from the Web TV website and stored.
howItWorks.step2Body: We transcribe the existing UN audio channels — the original "floor" mix and each official UN interpretation channel — directly. No machine translation is applied. Each channel is transcribed by a speech-to-text model chosen for that language.
howItWorks.step3Body: After transcription, a second AI model analyses the text and audio to assign names and affiliations to each speaker where possible. It uses contextual clues — such as the chair introducing delegates, country name mentions, and speaker diarization — together with the official list of participants when available.
howItWorks.step4Body: The transcript is automatically analysed to identify the main policy topics discussed, using categories relevant to UN proceedings (e.g. humanitarian affairs, international peace and security, human rights).
howItWorks.step5Body: Where official verbatim or summary records (PV/SR documents) exist, the system retrieves them and adds timestamps to align the text with the video. Besides timestamps, no AI processing is involved for these documents.

models.heading: Transcription model per language
models.intro: Different speech-to-text providers excel at different languages, so each track is routed to the model that performs best for it in our evaluation.
models.postProcessing: Post-processing — speaker identification and topic classification — is performed by Azure OpenAI GPT-5.5 for all languages.

accuracy.heading: Accuracy and limitations
accuracy.para1: These transcripts are created using automatic speech recognition and are not official UN records.
accuracy.para2: They are a faster, unofficial reference that may be useful for monitoring and research, but should not be cited as authoritative. For the official record, please refer to the <odsLink>UN Official Document System</odsLink> (verbatim records, summary records, and resolutions).
accuracy.issuesIntro: Automatic transcription is much faster than human transcription but introduces errors a human reviewer would catch. Common issues include:
accuracy.issue1: Proper nouns — country names, delegate names, place names, and UN document symbols may be misheard or misspelt
accuracy.issue2: Technical terminology — legal or procedural phrases specific to UN practice may be transcribed incorrectly
accuracy.issue3: Accented speech — accuracy varies by speaker accent and microphone quality
accuracy.issue4: Overlapping speech — when multiple speakers talk simultaneously, attribution may be wrong

sources.heading: Data sources
sources.webtvBody: — Meeting recordings and metadata, delivered via the Kaltura media platform (publicly accessible at webtv.un.org).
sources.odsBody: — Official verbatim records (PV documents) retrieved from documents.un.org where available.

status.heading: Status
status.body: This tool is in <publicPreview>Public Preview</publicPreview>. Features, coverage, and accuracy are actively being improved. Feedback is welcome.

experimental.heading: Experimental features
experimental.body: Experimental features (proposition analysis, speaker directory) are available to selected UN-system accounts during the preview period. To request access, please contact the maintainers.
